title: An engineered plasmid vector
caption: An engineered vector is a small circular DNA molecule with an origin of replication (so it is copied in the host), a selectable marker such as an ampicillin resistance gene, a multiple cloning site with unique restriction sites for inserting a gene, and sometimes a promoter to drive its expression. This map is illustrative, not a named plasmid.
alt: A circle labelled 3,000 base pairs with four coloured arcs: an origin of replication, an ampicillin resistance gene, a promoter and a short multiple cloning site with three unique cutting sites, EcoRI, BamHI and HindIII.
description: Origin of replication: the plasmid is copied independently in the host.
Selectable marker (here an ampicillin resistance gene): only cells that took up the plasmid grow on antibiotic.
Multiple cloning site: unique restriction sites for inserting a gene.
Promoter: drives expression of the inserted gene.
Digesting with two enzymes cuts out a small fragment; the fragments add up to the plasmid's length.
name: illustrative vector
